chunks: ʿAmr ibn Abī al-Miqdām narrated from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

In the wisdom of the family of Dāwūd عليه السلام, it is stated that the intelligent person should not set out in travel except for three things: provisioning for the Hereafter, mending one’s livelihood, or a pleasure that is not forbidden.

key_terms.الْعَاقِلِ: the intelligent or rational person who acts with sound judgment
key_terms.حِكْمَةِ: wisdom; a body of insightful moral teaching
key_terms.ظَاعِنًا: one setting out in travel or departing on a journey
key_terms.لِمَعَادٍ: for the return in the Hereafter; for one’s ultimate end before Allah
key_terms.مُحَرَّمٍ: that which is forbidden by the Sacred Law

ai.seo_question: For what reasons should a wise person travel according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that a wise person should travel with purpose and restraint. It identifies three sound motives for travel: preparing for the Hereafter, securing one’s livelihood, and enjoying lawful pleasure.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2386 - Amr ibn Abi Al-Miqdam narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) who said:

"In the wisdom of the family of Dawood (as) it is stated that it is incumbent upon the intelligent person not to travel except for one of three purposes: gathering provisions for the Hereafter, seeking sustenance for livelihood, or indulging in permissible pleasure."
